meta.scalability_note: 3 EU regions (Paris, Amsterdam, Warsaw); good horizontal auto-scaling for Kubernetes and serverless; GPU instances for AI; max 96 vCPUs (DEV1-XL equivalent); no global CDN edge network
meta.performance_note: 99.99% SLA for key services; ISO 27001 certified; multiple AZs per region; strong network backbone between EU datacenters; good serverless cold-start performance

AWS Amplify.note: No managed web/mobile application hosting platform. Apps deployed on VMs, containers, or Kubernetes.

AWS Lambda.note: Fully managed FaaS with Node.js, Python, Go, PHP, Rust runtimes. Auto-scaling to zero. GA service.

Amazon ECS.note: Managed container deployment via Serverless Containers (no cluster management) or Kapsule Kubernetes.

Amazon EKS.note: Fully managed Kubernetes with auto-upgrade, node pool auto-scaling, and multi-AZ support.

Amazon EC2.note: Diverse instance portfolio: development, general purpose, CPU-optimised, memory-optimised, GPU (H100, A100, L40S).

AWS Batch.note: Managed serverless batch job execution. Supports container-based workloads with scheduled and on-demand runs.

Amazon S3.note: S3-compatible object storage across all EU regions. Multi-AZ option available. Standard and Glacier-class tiers.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: Glacier storage class available in Object Storage. No dedicated archival product with retrieval SLAs.

Amazon EBS.note: High-performance SSD block volumes. Detachable from instances and snapshottable.

AWS Backup.note: Instance and volume snapshots available. No centralised cross-service backup policy management.

Amazon EFS.note: No managed elastic NFS-compatible shared file system.

Amazon RDS.note: Fully managed PostgreSQL and MySQL with automated backups, failover, and read replicas.

Amazon DocumentDB.note: Managed MongoDB in beta. Full compatibility and production SLAs still maturing.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed serverless NoSQL key-value database.

Amazon Timestream.note: No managed time-series database. Self-hosted InfluxDB or TimescaleDB is an option.

Amazon Aurora.note: No Aurora-equivalent high-performance managed relational DB.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: Managed Redis available in beta. Production readiness and full clustering features being finalised.

Amazon Redshift.note: No managed columnar data warehouse service.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: Fully managed HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with TLS termination, advanced routing, and health checks.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP mode available in the same Load Balancer product. Limited UDP and passthrough TLS options.

Amazon VPC.note: Full VPC with private networks, subnets, routing, and security groups (ACLs).

Amazon Route 53.note: Managed DNS with full record type support and TTL control. No advanced routing policies.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No native CDN service. Cloudflare or BunnyCDN used as third-party alternatives.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision API service.

Amazon SageMaker.note: Managed Jupyter notebooks and model inference endpoints available. No end-to-end MLOps pipeline.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed GenAI foundation model API. GPU instances available for self-hosted LLMs.

AWS Glue.note: No managed serverless ETL or data catalog service.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data cluster service.

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless SQL analytics over object storage.

AWS IAM.note: Full RBAC with users, groups, applications, and fine-grained resource policies. JWT-based API tokens.

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed user pool / app-level authentication service.

AWS KMS.note: Managed encryption key lifecycle management. Integrated with Object Storage and Block Storage.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: Fully managed secrets storage with versioning and API access. GA service.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: Managed TLS certificate provisioning via Load Balancers. Auto-renewal via ACME/Let's Encrypt.

AWS Security Hub.note: No centralised security posture management service.

AWS Config.note: No managed configuration compliance and drift detection.

AWS Shield.note: Basic network-level DDoS protection included. No advanced application-layer mitigation service.

AWS WAF.note: No managed Web Application Firewall service.

AWS CloudTrail.note: Audit trail of IAM and resource API actions. Beta service; limited retention and export options.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Managed Grafana dashboards and Loki-based log management via Cockpit. Less integrated than CloudWatch.

Amazon SNS.note: Alert notifications via Cockpit with webhook, email, and Slack integrations. No managed pub/sub at SNS scale.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Detailed cost breakdown and projected spend per resource and product in the console.

Amazon ECR.note: Fully managed Docker/OCI container registry with namespace isolation and retention policies.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No native IaC service. Official Scaleway Terraform provider available.

AWS IoT Core.note: Managed MQTT broker for IoT device connectivity. Supports routes to other Scaleway services. Less feature-rich than AWS IoT Core.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device registry or fleet management service.

Amazon SQS.note: Fully managed SQS-compatible message queuing. Also supports NATS and SNS-compatible pub/sub.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event bus or serverless event routing service.

Amazon SES.note: Fully managed transactional email with SMTP and API access. DKIM/SPF/DMARC support.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time data streaming service.
